Service is up (404 on `/` is expected — no root mapping). Now run the smoke test: login as admin, register a provider, validate it. Test scenarios:

1. Login admin/admin123 → token.
2. Register provider with baseUrl http://127.0.0.1:9090 (blocked by isUrlSafe) → validate → expect status ERROR with not-contacted message, lastValidatedAt set.
3. Register provider with unreachable public URL, e.g. http://nonexistent.invalid.example or http://192.0.2.1 (TEST-NET, site? 192.0.2.1 is not site-local per Java? isSiteLocalAddress covers 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16. 192.0.2.1 is not in those → passes isUrlSafe; connection will time out → -1 → phase 2 → -1 → ERROR "Connection failed"). But connect timeout 10s + read 10s, two phases → up to ~20-40s. The caller uses timeout=15. Hmm, for my smoke test I can use a URL that fails fast: DNS failure → UnknownHostException quickly → -1 fast. E.g. http://nonexistent-domain-xyz123.invalid — .invalid TLD fails DNS fast. isUrlSafe: InetAddress.getByName throws UnknownHostException → returns false! Wait — isUrlSafe returns false on UnknownHostException. So an unresolvable host is "unsafe" → not contacted. Hmm.

So to reach the contacted path, the host must resolve to a non-private, non-loopback address. In this sandbox, what resolves publicly? Maybe nothing (no external DNS?).
